title: Person overboard from a boat
version: Coastguard NZ 'What to do in an emergency' (web page, no date, footer 2026); Maritime NZ 'Radio a MAYDAY' (web page, no date); Greater Wellington Regional Council Harbours 'Wellington Skippers Cockpit Guide' (First edition, January 2023, PDF); Northland Regional Council 'Distress, urgency and calls' (web page, no date); Maritime NZ 'Surviving in cold water' (web page, no date); Water Safety New Zealand 'Cold water survival' (web page, no date, footer 2026); Tasman District Council 'Maritime accidents and responsibilities' (web page, no date); NOT NZ: Safe Transport Victoria (Australia) Recreational Boating Safety Handbook 'Person Overboard' (last modified 31 Jul 2023); NOT NZ: RYA (UK) 'Man overboard' (last updated 29 Oct 2025); all read 21 Nov 2026
sourceNote: Direct download was refused (proxy blocks coastguard.nz, maritimenz.govt.nz, gw.govt.nz, es.govt.nz, nrc.govt.nz, amsa.gov.au, rya.org.uk) and web search gave titles only, so every line was read by a fetch tool asked to quote exact lines in short pieces, rejoined. No PDF was in sources/. Sections: A Coastguard NZ (main source; A1 call VHF Ch16 or 111 and ask for Police, *500 non-urgent; A2 Mayday is for grave and imminent danger, person overboard is an example, 111 or Ch16; A3 example Mayday script; A4 wait for Coastguard Radio/Maritime Radio reply, relay calls; A5 four steps: shout loudly, throw life buoy/line/lifejacket to help them float and mark position, watch and don't take your eyes off them, stop the boat and turn back as soon as able, prop is a danger when approaching; A6 your life comes first; A7 report any accident to Maritime NZ). B Maritime NZ Radio a MAYDAY (B1 wear lifejacket and activate beacon first; B2 full power, VHF 16 or SSB 2182/4125/6215/8291 kHz; B3 call wording; B4-B6 listen, repeat, work through distress frequencies, tell shore station about EPIRB/PLB, follow instructions; heading says 'replay' [sic]). C Wellington Skippers Cockpit Guide 2023 (C1 Shout / Point even if you can't see them / Throw things that float to make a path back; avoid jumping in, if you must take flotation; C2 boat hook can help recover a person; C3 Mayday vs Pan-pan; C4 Ch16 or 111, *500 non-urgent; C5 overdue plan; C6 PLB 24 hours +, may sink, EPIRB 48 hours +, floats, accidental activation 0508 472 269; C7 1-3 hours with lifejacket, around 10 minutes without, heat lost 25 times faster in water, get out of water and wind, warm layers, children). D Northland RC (Mayday/Pan Pan definitions, cancel calls when over, other distress signals, SOS). E Maritime NZ cold water (cold water shock, drown in under 10 minutes, hypothermia signs, float first, get out of water, stay with boat, HELP and huddle postures; written for the person in the water). F Water Safety NZ (below 15°C, 1-3 min / up to 10 min / after 30 min, 1-10-1 guide, F5 when out of the water remove all wet clothing and warm in dry clothing or blankets: the only NZ aftercare line). G Tasman harbourmaster (report to Harbourmaster as soon as practicable for collision/sinking etc; report any accident or incident to Maritime Radio VHF 16 or RCCNZ 0508 222 433 immediately and to Maritime NZ within 24 hours). H NOT NZ Safe Transport Victoria (neutral and swing prop away, throw, point continuously, bearings on landmarks, GPS/chart plotter waypoint, bring alongside then stop engines, recover over the stern on a small boat, ladder, may be hurt/cold/exhausted). I NOT NZ RYA UK (less than 11 minutes on average in cold water, sometimes 4-5; spotter, danbuoy/life rings, MOB button on plotter for last known position, MAYDAY or DSC alert, stop or slow, approach from upwind, neutral or off alongside, heaving line, ladders/nets, unconscious casualty horizontal lift but recovery is the priority, onboard: monitor, first aid, risk of shock/hypothermia/secondary drowning, remove wet clothing, warm, take to medical facility). Not captured: the Maritime NZ Mayday sticker PDF; Environment Southland Safer Boating Guide (robots.txt unreachable); RYA sections on prevention and tethered (attached) person overboard (summary only, not copied); some joining punctuation in A2. Differences: (1) *500: Coastguard and Wellington say *500 is for non-urgent help and 111 for emergencies; Northland says 'All emergency distress calls - VHF channel 16 or phone *500'. (2) Mayday wording: Coastguard example says the boat name 3 times plus call sign, then 'Mayday' + name + call sign, position, problem, 'We require immediate assistance', number on board, 'Over'; Maritime NZ has the same order but puts beacon activation and lifejacket first and asks for assistance required and description of vessel/liferaft. (3) Immediate steps: Coastguard shout, throw, watch, stop and turn back; Wellington shout, point, throw (no 'stop/turn'); Victoria adds neutral and swing prop away; RYA adds MOB button and Mayday as immediate steps. (4) Survival times: Wellington 1-3 hours with lifejacket / around 10 minutes without; Maritime NZ drown in under 10 minutes; WSNZ 1-10-1 and hypothermia after 30 minutes / around an hour; RYA less than 11 minutes to recover before unresponsive. (5) Heat loss: Wellington 25 times faster in water; Maritime NZ 20 to 30 times. (6) Pan-pan: Wellington and Northland describe it for urgent but not life-threatening problems; Coastguard lists person overboard as a Mayday example; no source gives Pan-pan wording. Gaps: no NZ source names a turning/return manoeuvre (Williamson turn, figure-of-eight, quick stop etc.), and the non-NZ sources only say approach from upwind (RYA) or position alongside (Victoria); no NZ source mentions a GPS/MOB button or creating a waypoint (only non-NZ H and I); no source says to note the time the person went overboard; no NZ source says how to get the person back on board beyond 'boat hook' (Victoria: over the stern, ladder); no NZ source gives aftercare beyond WSNZ's one line, and none says to seek medical care afterwards (only RYA); no source says when to cancel a Mayday except Northland's general rule; no source lists what to record after a person overboard beyond the reporting duties (G, A7); no PLB/EPIRB step specific to a person in the water (only 'activate your distress beacon' before a Mayday).
status: Reviewer: 2 instructions missed and 14 findings, all fixed; gaps the sources leave open (turning back, recovery, aftercare, what to record). 87 of 87 quotes exact (web copy).
